text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore government to award two licences for local and international basic telecommunications services by mid-1998.
- Home Affairs Minister Wong Kan Seng says bomb shelters will be built in all underground Mass Rapid Transit stations along the North-east line.
- Japanese patrol ships repulse a flotilla of Taiwanese and Hongkong activists landing on disputed Diaoyu islands.
- Tender for two basic telecom licences likely to be hotly contested by more than 10 major local and foreign players.
- Judge delays sentencing tycoon George Tan in Hongkong's biggest corporate fraud trial.

- Singapore's largest insurance company, Great Eastern Life, to slash agents' commissions by 15 to 20 percent from Jan 1. - Malaysia records trade deficit in July of Malaysian $624.5 million after two straight months of trade surpluses, as imports rise and exports fall.

- Amtek Engineering reports 47 percent rise in group net earnings to Singapore $21.6 million for year ended June 30, 1996 and that its subsidiary, Microlite Electric Pte Ltd, would move vehicle electrical devices production to Pudong, China.
- Goldtron chairman Ong Soon Kiat says he has reduced his stake in the telecommunications firm to 19.12 percent from 23.9 percent.
- Singapore Telecom, Singapore CableVision and a subsidiary of the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore team up to form Singapore ONE venture with an investment of S$20 million.
- Hong Fok Corp reports group interim net earnings of S$9.12 million, mainly from sales of some factory units.
- Lum Chang subsidiary LC Development posts a 162 percent jump in group net profit to S$3.1 million for year ended June 30, 1996.
